facts.fact: The African Telecommunications Union Conference of Plenipotentiaries (CPL-26, Abuja, 23-24 July 2026) elected Eng. Kezias Kazuba Mwale of Zambia as Secretary General with 21 of 34 votes in the fourth round, to take office on 1 January 2027 for four years.

Zambia's Minister of Technology and Science, Felix C. Mutati, spoke at the close of the ATU Conference of Plenipotentiaries in Abuja, which Member States including Zambia's delegation attended on 23-24 July 2026.

facts.fact: Delegates at the ATU Conference of Plenipotentiaries (CPL-26, Abuja, closed 24 July 2026) elected Engr. Kezias Kazuba Mwale of Zambia as the Union's next Secretary-General with 21 of 34 votes in the final round, taking office on 1 January 2027 for four years.

The ATU's own release states that its Conference of Plenipotentiaries (Abuja, 23-24 July 2026) elected Eng. Kezias Kazuba Mwale of Zambia as Secretary General with 21 of 34 votes in the fourth round, to take office on 1 January 2027 for four years.
Zambia's Minister of Technology and Science, Felix C. Mutati, spoke at the ATU Conference of Plenipotentiaries in Abuja concluded on 24 July 2026.

Zambia's science and technology minister signed an ICT cooperation MoU with Angola's telecommunications minister at ANGOTIC 2023, covering AI, space technology and cross-border fibre.

facts.fact: ITWeb Africa reports Zambia and Burundi signed a memorandum of understanding at the Digital Government Africa Summit in Lusaka for a Lake Tanganyika fibre cable linking the two countries, with ministers of both countries quoted.

facts.fact: COMESA reports that Zambia hosted, with World Bank support, the 3-5 November 2026 Lusaka workshop at which 15 member states validated the Regional Digital Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan.

facts.fact: ZICTA says operators in the One Network Area, which includes Zambia, cut roaming tariffs by 3 to 93 percent and signed new bilateral roaming agreements.
BOCRA says Zambia implemented the One Network Area framework jointly with Botswana, with Botswana operators' roaming data prices to Zambian networks cut by 82% to 93%.
The African Mirror reports, citing BOCRA, that mobile operators in Zambia introduced roaming price cuts of 10 to 98.6 per cent under SADC's One Network Area.
Zambia's ministry partnered with Smart Africa on a national workshop under the AEDIB 2.0 programme, per Smart Africa.

note: Nothing stated on the country's regional policy action.
MoU is with UNDP, not an African body or government.
